html:
In November 1520 the Danish king Christian II, just crowned king of Sweden, had about eighty Swedish nobles, bishops and burghers executed in Stockholm's main square after a banquet.

Christian had conquered Sweden to restore the Kalmar Union under Danish control. He promised an amnesty, then had his opponents tried for heresy for having deposed the archbishop, and beheaded them over two days.

Instead of cowing Sweden, the massacre turned it against him. One of the dead was the father of the young noble Gustav Eriksson Vasa, who raised a revolt among the miners and farmers of Dalarna. By 1523 he was king as Gustav I, and Sweden had left the union for good. In Sweden Christian is remembered as Christian the Tyrant. See Sweden.
sum: In November 1520 the Danish king Christian II, just crowned king of Sweden, had about eighty Swedish nobles, bishops and burghers executed in Stockholm's main square after a banquet.
